defects: Missing [OpensMeasurableSpace α] hypothesis: without linking the topology and measurable space on α, the conclusion can fail (e.g. α with usual topology but trivial σ-algebra makes a continuous non-constant f fail to be measurable at all), so the produced statement is not merely differently shaped but actually false as stated
Missing [MeasurableSingletonClass α] hypothesis, needed so the countable exceptional set's points are measurable and f can be measurably spliced together with a limit of simple functions
Missing [SecondCountableTopologyEither α β] hypothesis, needed for strong measurability's approximation-by-simple-functions requirement

[PseudoMetricSpace β] is used instead of [PseudoMetrizableSpace β]; this bundles an explicit pseudometric rather than merely requiring the topology be pseudometrizable, which is a strictly stronger (less general) hypothesis, not just a different spelling of the same typeclass
